collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A grown villager's parent keeps telling them how to run their own household: set a boundary, or put up with it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) moved into (subject.his/her) own hut a year ago, and (friend), (subject.his/her) parent, has visited every single day: rearranging the pots, criticizing the roof, telling (subject) how to cook rice. (subject) loves (friend). (subject) is also going to scream. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) tells (friend), as kindly as (subject.he/she) can, that (subject.he/she) would like visits every few days, not every day, and the pots stay where they are. (friend) is wounded and goes home early. Then, three days later, (friend.he/she) visits, and does not touch the pots. It is very hard for (friend.him/her).

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) says nothing. The visits go on. The pots move. (subject) grits (subject.his/her) teeth. Then one day (friend) does not come, because (friend.he/she) is sick, and (subject) realizes how much (subject.he/she) misses it. (subject.He/she) still asks (friend.him/her) to leave the pots alone.
